_how_to_edit: Arm Lab (vibration test) data. Add a paddle to 'arm', 'offcenter' and/or 'stiffness', change 'updated', then run python3 build.py. Arm Score: higher = more arm-friendly, reference paddle = 100. Optional keys: photo (file in site/assets/paddles/product/), xray (slug in site/xray/), used, reference, second_tester (shows the 'Second tester' chip and the footnote in 'second_tester_note'), approx (stiffness value shown with ~).
arm_tested: Nov 21, 2026, one session (Franklin Whip: Nov 23, second tester)
headline: The Evolv (6 months of use) and the RPM Jade are the most arm-friendly so far; both Grit E2 CF versions are the firmest.
second_tester_note: Tested Nov 23, 2026 by a second tester (Daniel), with the Grit E2 CF reference in the same session. Its numbers are scaled to the reference so they line up with this table: compare them loosely. It ties the Grit overall: less shock and twist (it's heavier, swingweight 122 vs 110), but more buzz from its softer face.
offcenter_lead: Off-center hits sent 38–114% more shock to the wrist than center hits; the Evolvs were the most forgiving and the RPM Jade the least.
offcenter_notes: The RPM Jade is the cleanest paddle on center hits (1.16 g) but jumps the most on mishits, which fits its low twistweight.
Off-center hits mainly add jolt and twist, not more buzz.
These were small mishits during center blocks, so bigger mishits may be worse.
Early results: 7–8 hits per group, so treat small differences as ties.
offcenter_second_tester: Franklin Whip (second tester): off-center hits sent 40% more shock than center hits, the same as the Grit E2 CF in that session (+41%). It's shown as a note, not a row, because it was a different tester.
stiffness_title: RPM Jade has the stiffest face, Speedup Tide the softest

stiffness.flag: RPM Jade's buzz is dominated by a higher vibration mode; its value may overstate stiffness.

grip_test.title: Do grip upgrades protect your arm?
grip_test.lead: Our Nov 23 grip test: Daniel's Franklin Whip in 6 setups, with the Grit E2 CF reference at the start and end of the session (corrected for player fatigue). Arm Score: Grit E2 CF = 100.
rows: No change in shock; paddle twisted ~24% more in hand
No measurable benefit; adds ~17 g to the handle
Lead cut twist, no change in shock
grip_test.footnote: That run had softer ball contact, which inflates its score.
grip_test.takeaway: No grip upgrade reduced the shock or buzz reaching the wrist. Grips are about feel and fit, not shock protection. A little lead helped stability. For arm comfort, the paddle matters far more than the grip.
grip_test.limits: Limits: one player, one run per setup; sensors measure what reaches the wrist, not hand comfort.
